verdicts.evidence: `renderEuAiAct` is reachable only through `complianceCommand` with key 'eu-ai-act' (the REGIMES table in src/commands/compliance.ts), and its `lens` argument comes only from `loadRegime('eu-ai-act', opts.regimeVersion)`, which reads `regimes/<regime>@<version>.json` out of the packaged REGIMES_DIR and THROWS (the caller maps it to exit 2) on any version not shipped. Two eu-ai-act lenses ship - 2024-1689 and 2026-1744 - and both define `highRisk {bindFrom, scope}`, `articles.runtimeLogging` and the nine-row `annexIv`. PROBE: with the mutant applied the rendered document is byte-identical on both fixtures (fresh `runward init` mission and examples/request-triage/runward), so the guard never fires on any reachable input. SENSITIVITY CONTROL: on a lens with no `highRisk` key the two WOULD differ - the shipped code interpolates the literal `**undefined**` as the date on which high-risk obligations bind, the mutant throws a TypeError instead. That input cannot occur: (a) loadRegime accepts only the shipped filenames and refuses anything else with the shipped list; (b) test/unit/regimes.test.js refuses any stray file in regimes/ that is not `<known-regime>@<version>.json`; (c) test/unit/compliance.test.js asserts `!md.includes("undefined")` on the default eu lens together with the exact `bind from\n> **2 December 2027 (Annex III) / 2 August 2028 (Annex I)**` block and all nine `| N. ` Annex IV rows, so a future lens dropping a key reddens the unit suite before it can reach a user. Filed defence-in-depth rather than equivalent because the mutant is not semantically equivalent on the guarded input - it is only unreachable. Note the direction, since it matters to a regulated reader: on the guarded input the MUTANT is the safer of the two - it fails loudly where the shipped code prints 'undefined' into a legal date field.
